subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept a longer derived isolated-cron setup watchdog window for long `agentTurn` jobs, or require a different operator-tunable policy before fixing this issue?
rationale: Current main still has the fixed 60s pre-runner watchdog, but changing it affects cron capacity when setup is genuinely stuck, so the remaining blocker is maintainer acceptance of that availability tradeoff.

options.title: Accept bounded derived setup watchdog
options.body: Land the open PR or equivalent so long isolated `agentTurn` jobs can spend more than 60s in setup while still capped by job timeout policy.

options.title: Require configurable watchdog policy
options.body: Pause the current PR path and define a documented cron configuration knob with migration and operator guidance before changing default setup timing.

options.title: Keep 60s fail-fast behavior
options.body: Reject longer setup waits and keep this issue open only for better diagnostics or provider-specific startup fixes.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived setup watchdog
recommendation.body: Land the open PR or equivalent so long isolated `agentTurn` jobs can spend more than 60s in setup while still capped by job timeout policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the adjacent setup-timeout restart behavior and touched the same watchdog/timer boundary.
